mnemonic: You do not simply say it, you sit down and write it out and post it, because that is what the teacher is owed: おれい.
notes: 礼 on its own is the bow and the courtesy behind it. Near 綺麗 きれい and 重い おもい in sound and nothing else.
sentence: 先生にお礼の手紙を書きました。
sentence_meaning: I wrote a letter of gratitude to my teacher.

mnemonic: After 後 the event, and the heart 忄 goes back over it every 毎 single time. No use to anybody, and it happens anyway: こうかい.
sentence: 後悔しても、しょうがない。
sentence_meaning: Even if you have regrets, there's nothing you can do.

mnemonic: Two characters for the same wanting stacked up, and what he wants is a desk at head office. Nobody has said yes yet: きぼう.
sentence: 彼は本社で働くことを希望しています。
sentence_meaning: He hopes to work at the head office.

meaning: to come down, to hang down, to fall
mnemonic: Whatever was up comes down 下 on its own, and the thermometer finally agrees with everybody. Nobody pulled it down: さがる.
notes: 上がる あがる is the same movement the other way. 下りる おりる is coming down off something and 落ちる おちる is falling. 秋 あき is the other fall, the season.
sentence: やっと熱が下がった。
sentence_meaning: His fever finally went down.

mnemonic: You point yourself in the one direction 方 and turn up at the far end of it with something to say 言. Kyoto, in the summer: おとずれる.
sentence: 私は夏に京都を訪れました。
sentence_meaning: I visited Kyoto this summer.

mnemonic: He worked harder than anybody all term and somebody finally said so out loud, with the rest of them standing there: ほめる.
sentence: 頑張ったので褒められました。
sentence_meaning: He was praised because he worked hard.

mnemonic: What you were born with, held up against 格 what everybody else was born with. Mine and my sister's came out opposite ways: せいかく.
notes: 人物 じんぶつ is a person who counts for something. 性格 is what somebody is actually like.
sentence: 僕と姉の性格は正反対です。
sentence_meaning: My personality and my elder sister's are the exact opposite.

mnemonic: A copy of the true 真 thing, made by holding still and pressing once. This one has the whole family in it: しゃしん.
sentence: これは家族の写真です。
sentence_meaning: This is a photograph of my family.

mnemonic: The grass 艹 that brings ease 楽, ground down and put in a bottle. Take it, and do not skip a day: くすり.
sentence: この薬を必ず飲んでください。
sentence_meaning: Please be sure to take this medicine.

mnemonic: The formal way of saying it, friend 友 with person 人 bolted on, and the two of them have known each other since school: ゆうじん.
notes: 友達 ともだち is what you actually say out loud. 友人 is for writing, and for talking about somebody rather than to them.
sentence: 彼は高校時代からの友人です。
sentence_meaning: He's my old friend from high school.

mnemonic: Back when he was still a student, which was long enough ago that it wants saying in a different tense: かつて.
notes: Near 勝手 かって in sound only. 一度 いちど is once as in one time. かつて is once as in back then.
sentence: かつて私が学生だった頃のことです。
sentence_meaning: That was when I was still a student.

mnemonic: Certain 確 and real 実 both at once, which is more certainty than most things ever get. She will be president: かくじつ.
sentence: 彼女が将来、大統領になることは確実です。
sentence_meaning: It is certain that she will become the president in the future.

mnemonic: There was a point where he needed the help and it has gone by. Not yet, and not any more either: もはや.
notes: もう and 既に すでに are already. もはや leans on it being too late for the thing to matter now.
sentence: もはや彼の助けは必要じゃないの。
sentence_meaning: His help is no longer needed.

mnemonic: The typhoon takes itself off 去 somewhere else and the wind drops behind it. Gone, and the going is the whole point: さる.
sentence: 台風が去って風が静まったね。
sentence_meaning: The typhoon has passed and the wind has dropped.

mnemonic: One 一 section 部 of it and the rest left exactly alone. Change that much of the plan and the plan still stands: いちぶ.
notes: 部分 ぶぶん is a part in general. 一部 is one part of a thing, with the remainder still there.
sentence: 計画を一部変更しましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's change part of the plan.

mnemonic: Far enough down the road that you would have to think about it first, and once in a while that is precisely the appeal: とおく.
sentence: たまには遠くへ行きたいです。
sentence_meaning: At times, I like to travel far away.

mnemonic: The flesh 月 that gives out first when you have been laughing for ten minutes and it is still going: はら.
sentence: 笑いすぎて腹が痛い。
sentence_meaning: I laughed so much that my belly hurts.

mnemonic: Everybody 皆 goes up the hill 阝 a step 段 at a time and there is no other way up it. Over there, on the left: かいだん.
sentence: 階段はあそこです。
sentence_meaning: The stairs are over there.

mnemonic: The turning that suits 適 where you are going, landed on square 当. There was no answer to that question that fitted: てきとう.
notes: Careful in speech, where 適当 often means the opposite, done any old how and not properly. Context decides which.
sentence: その質問の適当な答えが見つかりません。
sentence_meaning: I could not find an appropriate answer to that question.

mnemonic: It comes up out of the mouth when the doctor asks, and it is the one part of you that you cannot get a look at yourself: した.
notes: Same reading as 下 した, under. 下 is a mark below a line. This is the thing in your mouth, and it sits inside 話 talk.
sentence: 舌を出してください。
sentence_meaning: Stick out your tongue.

mnemonic: What takes shape in your head 想 in advance 予, and then the thing happens and you turn out to have had it right: よそう.
notes: 期待 きたい is expectation as hoping for something. 予想 is expectation as a forecast.
sentence: 私の予想が当たった。
sentence_meaning: What I expected was right.

mnemonic: Something goes up 興 in front of them and a big 大 bird 隹 comes off the field 田 all at once. The crowd was out of its seats: こうふん.
sentence: 観客は興奮していたよ。
sentence_meaning: The spectators were excited.

mnemonic: The gate 関 is what ties your side to theirs, and whatever stands on the other one is now your business too. His work touches the military: かかわる.
sentence: 彼は軍事に関わる仕事を続けてきたんだ。
sentence_meaning: He's been working a military-related job.

mnemonic: The sun coming up over the edge of things and everything gone pale in it. It is the colour snow comes in: しろ.
notes: Same reading as 城 しろ, castle. 白い しろい is the adjective, and this is the colour as a noun.
sentence: 白は雪の色です。
sentence_meaning: White is the color of snow.

mnemonic: The bird 隹 carries on down the road 辶 because somebody behind it moved it along. Let us get through the lesson: すすめる.
notes: The pair works the usual way round. 進む すすむ is a thing going forward by itself and 進める is you pushing it on.
sentence: 早く授業を進めましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's hurry up and proceed with our class.

mnemonic: A true 真 blade 剣 and not a wooden one, which is the whole difference between practice and meaning it. He listened like that: しんけん.
notes: 大変 たいへん is serious as in a big deal. 真剣 is serious as in in earnest.
sentence: 彼は真剣に話を聞いていました。
sentence_meaning: He listened earnestly to the story.

meaning: to press, to close in on
mnemonic: The road 辶 narrows down to a white 白 line and whatever is at the end of it is not slowing. The deadline is Friday: せまる.
sentence: 締め切りが迫っています。
sentence_meaning: The deadline is approaching.

mnemonic: Two lines left on the last page and then he is done. Not finished, but near enough that he is saying so: ほぼ.
notes: ほとんど is almost as in nearly all of it. ほぼ is closer to roughly, and it goes in front of numbers.
sentence: 仕事がほぼ終わりました。
sentence_meaning: My work is almost finished.

mnemonic: Not about thirty thousand. Thirty thousand, to the yen, with nothing to round off in either direction: ちょうど.
sentence: 値段はちょうど3万円です。
sentence_meaning: The price is exactly 30,000 yen.

mnemonic: A question 問 you are asking because you do not believe the answer, which is a different thing from wanting information: ぎもん.
notes: 問題 もんだい is a problem or a question on paper and 質問 しつもん is a question you put to somebody. 疑問 is a doubt.
sentence: 彼の言葉が本当かは疑問です。
sentence_meaning: I doubt whether what he says is true.

mnemonic: Somebody points 指 at the thing and shows 示 you what is to be done with it, and you go on exactly as told: しじ.
sentence: 指示されたとおりに進んでください。
sentence_meaning: Please proceed as instructed.

mnemonic: The wind gets into the branches and the whole tree goes over and comes back, over and back, and nobody laid a hand on it: ゆれる.
sentence: 風で木が揺れています。
sentence_meaning: The trees are swaying in the wind.

mnemonic: One thing set against 相 another and landing square 当 on it. A pound comes out at four hundred and fifty four grams: そうとう.
sentence: 1ポンドは454グラムに相当します。
sentence_meaning: One pound is equivalent to 454 grams.

mnemonic: A frame with strings across it, music, and the ease that comes with it. The chair you want at home is the same idea: らく.
notes: Read らく it is easy and comfortable, and in 楽しい たのしい it is enjoyable. 簡単 かんたん is easy as in not difficult, 楽 is easy as in not hard work.
sentence: 家で休むのに楽な椅子が欲しいです。
sentence_meaning: I want a comfortable chair to rest in at home.

mnemonic: You went on feel 勘 instead of checking, and the feel was wrong 違. You turned up at two and it had been at one: かんちがい.
sentence: 待ち合わせは2時だと勘違いしていました。
sentence_meaning: I mistakenly thought the meeting was at two o'clock.

mnemonic: A word 言 of warning and a weapon kept ready 戒 rather than used. After the earthquake, watch the water: けいかい.
sentence: 地震のあとは津波に警戒してください。
sentence_meaning: Beware of tsunamis after an earthquake.

meaning: to check, to make sure of
mnemonic: You have written it and you believe it is right, and believing is not the same as being certain 確. Read it again: たしかめる.
notes: 確か たしか on its own hedges, fairly sure. 確かめる is going and making it certain.
sentence: レポートを書いたら、確かめてください。
sentence_meaning: Once you've written your report, please check it.

mnemonic: A crescent with a couple of strokes through it, and tonight it is bright enough to read a paper by: つき.
notes: Read げつ it is the month, and Monday. Squeezed onto the left of a character it usually stands for flesh instead.
sentence: 今晩は月が明るく見えます。
sentence_meaning: You can see the moon brightly tonight.

meaning: to doubt, to be suspicious of
mnemonic: You stop at the fork and take neither road, because you have stopped being sure the person giving the directions meant well: うたがう.
sentence: なぜあなたは私を疑うのですか。
sentence_meaning: Why do you doubt me?

mnemonic: Talk 話 sent down a wire on lightning 電, which is what it actually is, and you rang your mother on one: でんわ.
sentence: 母と電話で話しました。
sentence_meaning: I spoke with my mother on the phone.

mnemonic: It got there 成 and it got longer 長 while nobody was watching it do either. The tree is over the fence now: せいちょう.
sentence: 庭の木、大きく成長したわね。
sentence_meaning: The tree in the garden has grown a lot.

mnemonic: Metal 金 taken down to an edge that is through your finger before the pain has caught up. You look down and there is blood: するどい.
sentence: 鋭い刃物で指を怪我した。
sentence_meaning: I injured my finger with a sharp knife.

mnemonic: A statement 言 that is correct 正 and something solid to stand it on 拠. No arrest until both of those turn up: しょうこ.
sentence: 証拠を見つけるまで逮捕はできません。
sentence_meaning: It is not possible to make an arrest until evidence is found.

mnemonic: You thread 糸 the two of them together and stand in the middle 介 while they shake hands. This is my friend, this is my teacher: しょうかい.
sentence: 先生に友達を紹介します。
sentence_meaning: I will introduce my friend to the teacher.

mnemonic: The real 実 thing at the exact edge 際 where it meets you, rather than the version in the description. He is not that tall: じっさい.
notes: 現実 げんじつ is reality as the whole state of things. 実際 is in actual fact, set against whatever was claimed.
sentence: 彼は実際にはあまり背が高くない。
sentence_meaning: In reality, he's not very tall.

mnemonic: Whatever 何 it happens to be, no shortlist and no exceptions. She takes the lot to her mother: なんでも.
sentence: 私は母に何でも相談しています。
sentence_meaning: I consult with my mother about everything.

mnemonic: Making 作 things as a trade 業, hands on it and taking up room while you do. He needs more space than this: さぎょう.
notes: 仕事 しごと is your job and 働く はたらく is the verb, to work. 作業 is the physical work being done, the operation itself.
sentence: 作業するにはもっと広いスペースが必要だ。
sentence_meaning: I need a bigger space to work.

mnemonic: Heavy 重 and needed 要 at the same time, which between them is what important amounts to. Do not lose that document: じゅうよう.
sentence: これは重要な書類です。
sentence_meaning: This is an important document.

mnemonic: Metal 金 cut to a shape that opens one door in the world and no other, and it lives in a coat pocket: かぎ.
sentence: これはアパートの鍵です。
sentence_meaning: This is the key to the apartment.

mnemonic: Two things arrive at the one point 衝 and something is struck 撃 hard enough to be felt across the room. The news landed like that: しょうげき.
sentence: 衝撃のニュースが飛び込んできた。
sentence_meaning: The shocking news filled the airwaves.
